To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the immunosuppressant CsA induces proliferation of human pulmonary arterial smooth muscle cells (PASMCs), which can be inhibited by anti-ET-1 antibodies, the calcium channel blocker VP, and the somatostatin analogue SDT, but not by the CsA analogue SDZ IMM 1.
the new hydroxyethyl cyclosporine derivative SDZ IMM 25 is a less potent inducer of proliferation of pulmonary artery smooth muscle (PASMCs) than CsA.
CsA induced a concentration-dependent stimulation of proliferation of human PASMCs, and that the latter effect was mediated by ET-1.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the mechanisms of the immunosuppessive CsA on the proliferation of PASMC, which is involved in pulmonary hypertension.
the development of new immunosuppressive drugs, such as SDZ IMM 126, which do not have the side effect of inducing smooth muscle cell proliferation in pulmonary artery.
the development of new immunosuppressive agents with fewer side-effects than CsA.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the immunosuppressant drug CsA increases the rate of proliferation in human PASMCs.
CsA induces proliferation of PASMC by a mechanism involving the ET-1 receptor.
CsA-induced PASCM proliferation was mediated by an increased ET-1 secretion from endothelial cells, and that this effect was antagonised by SDT, VP, or anti-ET-1 antibodies.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
CsA induced a proliferation of human PASMCs, probably by inducing ET-1 release from the endothelium.
CsA is a potent stimulator of human PASMC proliferation and that this action can be antagonized by anti-ET-1 antibodies, VP, and octreotides.
CsA-induced PASM proliferation is ET-1 dependent.
The main takeaway from our work is that
CsA increases the rate of proliferation in PASMCs and that this effect is mediated, at least in part, by the release of the potent vasoactive peptide ET-1, which in turn stimulates cell growth.
CsA induces PASMC proliferation through an ET-1-dependent mechanism.
ET-1 may play an important role in CsA-induced PASM proliferation.
